style: Small 16:9 flat editorial illustration accompanying a faakt.io mobile card. Choose a simple motif appropriate to the article: a recognizable subject, object, person, action, concise metaphor or immediately readable scientific relationship. Invite reading through a striking subject, gesture, atmosphere or visual contrast. Readability alone is insufficient: even one arrow between a few detached objects can feel like an equation of inputs and outputs. Prefer a coherent scene or natural encounter when it carries the idea better; connect elements through pose, gaze, movement or shared space rather than lining up ingredients and results. Diagrams, arrows and illustrated principles remain welcome when their visual form is itself expressive and suited to the article. Judge the whole composition, not just the number of objects or steps. A simple explanatory contrast or interaction is welcome when understood at a glance. If explanation would require many separate objects, several steps or arrows tracing which part implies the next, choose one recognizable aspect instead. The text explains the science and story; the picture does not need to explain the mechanism, prove the claim or summarize the whole article. A standalone relevant object is enough. Examples: a moving ambulance for Doppler effect; a book with a prohibition sign for a banned novel; a pulsar with a simple beam, without Earth, waveform, magnetic field or observation equipment. Metadata is context, not a checklist of objects to draw. Omit secondary subjects and explanatory marks when the main motif already works. Choose between a simple accompanying subject and a simple explanatory relationship according to context. A compact comparison or a useful single arrow is fine; avoid multistep experiments, networks of implications and inventories of disconnected scientific components. A small supporting symbol is welcome when immediately readable. Broad clean silhouettes, aim for 5-8 large flat shapes, at most 3 muted foreground colors and at least one third empty transparent space. Recognizable at 160x90 and clean at 320x180 on both the base dark card (#141414 to #0d0d0d) and a CSS-owned irregular multicolor glow: four asymmetrically sized radial gradients from the card corners in three hues from the metadata palette, combined layer opacity 10%, fading fully toward the darkest card center. Separate the main silhouette and essential internal features from these colored areas through lightness as well as hue. Use sufficiently opaque foreground shapes; avoid near-black silhouettes, faint thin details and same-value edges that vanish against a related glow color. Keep meaningful light or mist forms readable without adding decorative effects. Do not paint the card glow or a compensating opaque panel into the asset. Optically center the complete main motif in the full canvas with balanced transparent margins; do not reserve an empty text column. Use off-center placement only when necessary for the specific meaning, interaction or direction of action. Centering does not require mirrored or rigidly symmetric objects. At most one flat shadow plane; no realistic lighting, reflections, grain, fine textures, tiny repeated details, decorative scenery, 3D or photorealism. Preserve factual identity and avoid visible contradictions, but leave qualifications and explanations to the article. Default to no text; never add a caption merely naming the pictured object. No legends, axes, connectors or numerical readouts just for completeness. Restrained grown-up magazine artwork. Genuinely transparent background: no backdrop rectangle, black or near-black fill, dark gradient, vignette, decorative glow, border or edge color. Empty areas and corners must be transparent so the card shows through. Preserve alpha. If transparency is technically impossible, use only the supplied exact uniform fallback color. Soft translucent forms are allowed when the selected subject is light or mist, never as a backdrop.

art.concept: Two Napoleonic sailing warships crossing at close quarters, with clearly perpendicular headings.
An exhausted early nineteenth century draft horse in a simple artillery harness, head lowered.
A Chappe optical telegraph tower with the characteristic articulated semaphore arms.
An early nineteenth century civil code book with a wedding ring resting on its closed cover; no readable text.
A few Napoleonic infantry silhouettes sheltering immediately behind a broad ridge.
An open reference book beside a magnifying glass, a simple accompaniment to document retrieval.
A small and a larger processor side by side jointly reviewing one short strip of token tiles.
A light colored padlock with a restrained lattice pattern on its body, accompanying lattice cryptography.
A simple cutaway of a two-layer tandem solar cell receiving a single broad band of light.
A simple battery cutaway exposing a porous carbon electrode, without elemental labels.
A modest piece of bread and a cup of water as sufficient satisfaction of basic needs.
A balance scale with a hand returning one displaced weight to restore equilibrium.
An open hand gently stops a second clenched hand; a concise refusal of retaliation.
An overturned ancient wine cup beside a hesitant hand, accompanying culpable ignorance.
An ancient Greek philosopher sets a crown aside while considering a civic responsibility.
An empty royal throne, accompanying a definite description that lacks a referent.
An ordinary person stands at an open gate holding their own reins as a compact metaphor for two liberties.
Hands test the load on a simple bridge model, accompanying inquiry through active testing.
Two broad overlapping horizon frames become one shared view, accompanying historically situated understanding.
An anonymous person in a simple room sorts a few cards with invented abstract marks, no real language text.
A small irregular asteroid recoils from an asymmetric fan of ejected debris after a probe impact.
A dark asteroid sample grain held inside a clean open sample capsule.
A star behind a gas giant; a single broad band of light passes through the atmospheric rim, no extra diagram.
A small space probe curves around one planet, one subtle trajectory curve, no arrows or labels.
IKAROS with a single square thin solar sail and small central spacecraft, isolated without scenery.
A lonely fictional Frankenstein creature reaches toward a door from which its creator has departed; no film likeness.
A solitary nineteenth century student sits hunched with a stark divided shadow, accompanying guilt.
A nineteenth century woman leaves a dollhouse-like doorway carrying a small travel bag.
A youthful Victorian portrait whose painted face has a subtly corrupted half, one framed portrait only.
An anonymous hand offers one tablet in front of a few identical hatchery bottles, accompanying manufactured contentment.
A Soviet-era tank faces one simple Budapest street barricade in 1956, no flags or crowds.
A Soviet-era tank tread presses a newspaper in a Czechoslovak street, accompanying August 1968.
Two simple porcelain tea cups face each other across a diplomatic table, accompanying the opening to China.
A simplified historically recognizable La Moneda palace facade with a small plume of smoke, no people.
A lowered red Soviet flag with a small hammer and sickle near a bare pole, accompanying the end of the USSR.
Two ordinary partners in one conversation; one leans forward to speak while the other turns away.
Two hands repair one broken ceramic cup, accompanying an apology with concrete repair.
One ordinary partner warmly thanks the other while acknowledging a small helpful gesture.
An ordinary couple learn a simple dance step together with curious engaged expressions.
Two tired partners talk across a small table, one rubbing a sleepy eye; no clocks or extra symbols.
